Apple's defense in the US v. Google antitrust trial includes arguments about user experience, privacy, and the necessity of Google's services in Apple's ecosystem. Key points include:

  • Apple argues against offering users a choice of search engines during setup due to the potential for a poor user experience.
  • Apple maintains that Google is the best search engine and has better privacy practices compared to competitors.
  • Apple emphasizes the seamless integration of Google services into its platform, citing historical innovations like the URL and search bar combination in Safari.
# See also * [Google's AI Practices and Antitrust Suit Against News Publishers](google-s-ai-practices-and-antitrust-suit-against-news.md) - A class action lawsuit filed by news publishers accuses Google and Alphabet of anticompetitive practices, particularly regarding AI technologies used in Google's Search Generative Experience (SGE) and Bard AI chatbot. The lawsuit alleges misuse of publishers' content and ad revenue, and seeks an injunction to prevent improper use of publisher data for AI training. * [Google's Attempts to Preinstall Services on iPhones](../ai-startups-gd/google-s-attempts-to-preinstall-services-on-iphones.md) - Google proposed preinstalling Google services on every iOS device in 2018, aiming for mutual benefits with Apple. However, Apple declined the offer. * [Google Search Operations and User Data Handling](../ai-search/google-search-operations-and-user-data-handling.md) - Discusses Google's operations in search, including keyword matching, ad systems, and user data handling. Highlights the increase in data volume and the changes in search behavior over time.
